issues.text: CLAIMS OF ISS-0093, one by one (commands and output in self_check). (1) store.js:395 `const masked = maskSecrets(content)` in #publish: CONFIRMED; all three entries (writeResultFile, importWorkFile, importResultBytes) go through it. (2) runner.js:132 depsOf: CONFIRMED, and it is a second, independent masking of the same text (R5): depsOf re-masks the file it reads from files/; it feeds the work runs (defaultContext, engine.js:458, 591, 667), the task check and the goal check (review.js:55, 72). (3) M7 'any x.y.z' mask.js:104-117: CONFIRMED with an edge: exactly three non-empty parts; `a.b` and `a.b.c.d` are not touched, a trailing dot is punctuation (so `this.state.files.length` survives and `obj.prop.method()` does not). (4) M10 mask.js:242-269: DIFFERENT - it is real (lockfile integrity strings, long mixed-case identifiers: R3) but it made 0 of the marks in the five named files and 0 in all 149 files of tools/src; the named corruption is M7 alone. (5) Counts 3, 7, 52, 5, 196: CONFIRMED as marks in the masked output; for pixel-office/public/app.js 1 of the 196 is a literal label already in the source, masking added 195. None of the five files holds a secret: M1-M6, M8, M9 together change none of them. (6) Sample lines and the version line: CONFIRMED. (7) Deletion of the unmasked source, runner.js 655-687 (the comment at 655, removeSource 666-687) and README.md:391: CONFIRMED, but DIFFERENT in meaning: it is the recorded rule (decisions/0018 P6; REQ-010 criterion 16; REQ-013 criteria 14 and 15 say 'this rule remains'; decision 0035 kept it), pinned by RF-03, SF-13, EX-41; it is harmless on its own, and harmful only together with the corruption - after the run `work/` is empty and no file of the project folder holds `a.b.c` (R4). (8) Reviewer and dependents get the broken text: CONFIRMED (R4 reviewer stdin, R5). (9) No message to the user: CONFIRMED - RESULT_FILE carries only name, bytes, sha256, kind, from_work; no event of the run mentions masking (R4). (10) 'The role Разработчик has Write/Edit and returns code': DIFFERENT - all ten roles have Write and Edit (role-internal.js:9); the developer prompt asks for technical solutions and descriptions in text; the damage is not about code: any result file with a three-part token is hit (hosts, versions like 22.21.1, names like a.test.js), as the researcher file of REAL-20261013-01 already showed (ISS-0058). (11) The owner's probe of 2026-10-27 with 41 marks: NOT VERIFIABLE - no artifact of it in the project, only the audit text; my numbers agree in kind. (12) 'REQ-009 criterion 12': DIFFERENT - criterion 12 is about the events CHAT and task data and says nothing of result files; masking of the content of a result file is required by REQ-010 criterion 16(б) and described in tools/README.md:253; and NO criterion or test says that ordinary content of a result file must stay unchanged (see I9).

CAUSE. One mechanism (maskSecrets of tools/src/pixel-office/mask.js, rules M1-M10, written by decision 0013 for short lines of the owner's requests, where 'extra masking is the safe side') was reused for a different kind of data, the full text of files, by decision 0017 (P9: only masked text goes to files/) without a separate analysis of what masking does to code. The error is born in mask.js (maskThreeParts, lines 108-117: any run of exactly three dotted parts), reached through two calls: store.js:395 (#publish, on write) and runner.js:132 (depsOf, on every read for a prompt). Rule broken: no written rule forbids it (that is the gap, I9); the effect breaks the intent of REQ-010 16(б)/REQ-013 14-15 (the reviewer and the dependents work on the file) and quality-bar Q10 (ordinary input - code - breaks the result with no understandable message). Why the tests did not catch it: (a) every guard test uses a key bait (`ghp_...`, a JWT) and checks only that the bait is gone - none checks that the rest of the file is kept; (b) TM-43 'masking does not touch ids, codes, hashes and names' writes the content `Версия 1.2.3` (which M7 turns into `Версия [скрыто]`) and asserts only the name, the hash shape and the ids, never the content; (c) TM-43 first test and TM-58 use the function under test as the oracle (`maskSecrets(text)`, the hash of the masked file), so a rule that over-masks is 'right' by construction; (d) TM-44 pins that the team core imports the one function and has no rules of its own, which is right for secrets but made 'one function for lines and for files' look intended.

PLACES OF THE SAME KIND - full text of a file goes through maskSecrets. (a) tools/src/team/store.js:395 #publish (entries writeResultFile 418, importWorkFile 424, importResultBytes 443) - reproduced (R4). (b) tools/src/team/runner.js:132 depsOf - reproduced (R5); callers: runner.js:145 (defaultContext), review.js:55 and 72, engine.js:458/591/667. Those are the only two places where the content of a result file meets the masking; every other reader of files/ goes through depsOf. Not of the kind (checked by reading): web/display.js resultRef (names and links only, no content), team/view.js, cli.js (no content), executor.js buildPrompt (takes dep.content already prepared by depsOf), acceptedFilesText (names only, not masked), single-run.js importOutputs (only passes bytes to importResultBytes, i.e. place (a); it has no work/ source and no deletion, so there is nothing to share with runner.js removeSource).

PLACES THAT USE THE SAME RULES ON SHORT LINES OF TEXT and must keep their masking (decisions 0013, 0056; ISS-0058 family, not part of ISS-0093): team journal text fields - store.js:221 (#append, mapTextFields over every text field of every event), store.js:556 (createProject goal), store.js:310, engine/channel.js:246/321/323, engine/commands.js:133 (length checks of masked text; note M7 can make a 5-character `a.b.c` 8 characters long), runner.js:97 and engine/single-run.js:17 (prepareText of an agent event text, summary and memory text - runner.js:267, 380, 390; single-run.js:120, 220: model-written prose, same false positives as ISS-0058). Pixel Office: pixel-office/protocol.js:75 maskField (description, roles), :97 prepareText (owner request), :227 maskSecrets(prompt_text); pixel-office/server.js:351 (note_text); pixel-office/note.js:108. Planner: engine/plan.js:313 acceptedBlock masks the names of accepted files line by line - a name with three parts (app.test.js, plan.v2.md) is hidden for the planner (R7) although names are checked by pattern and by 0017 P8 are not masked; this is ISS-0045/ISS-0058 (names), not ISS-0093. The picker (picker/places.js HIDDEN) has its own mechanism and does not import mask.js. `grep` over the whole repository outside tools/src, tools/test, docs, handoffs, decisions finds no other user of mask.js.

SIMILAR DEFECTS. No closed defect has the same cause, so this is not a return of an earlier cause and the severity rule 'not below MEDIUM for a return' does not apply. Related: ISS-0068 (closed 2026-10-14) made description and role pass maskSecrets - it widened the reach of M7/M10 but is a different cause (a gap in masking). ISS-0023 (closed 2026-10-11) and decision 0035 kept the deletion of the source and added the name mapping - the deletion is a recorded rule. ISS-0065 is NOT about masking (it is the real clock in channel tests, open). Open and on the same function: ISS-0058 (M7 hosts, file names in descriptions, M10 on long roles), ISS-0045 (names of accepted files; maskSecrets does not hide `preghp_...`, acceptedBlock masks names). ISS-0025/0040/0024 (work/ collisions, review context, files of all attempts) are about work/ and files/ but not about content.

TESTS THAT PIN THE CURRENT BEHAVIOUR (found by mutation, R6; all in the set that ran and passed 548/548 on the base). Pin 'a secret in a result file is replaced by the label and the file is accepted': TM-57 (team-store.test.js:499, work/ -> files/, also 'work/ is not changed' and the original keeps its content), TM-58 (:757, the hash in the journal is the hash of the masked file, `notEqual` to the hash of the raw text), TM-63 (:1006, importResultBytes), TM-43 first test (team-journal.test.js:450, a JWT, an sk-ant key, ghp, AKIA and `password=` in a result file; oracle `maskSecrets(text)`), EX-41 (exec-workdir.test.js) and EX-51 (exec-scripted-source.test.js:71), RF-03 (team-engine-reads-files.test.js:134, also pins: source removed, `readdirSync(work)` equals [], no copy anywhere, modes), SF-13 (team-engine-rounds.test.js:234, same). Only TM-43 depends on M7 (the JWT bait); none depends on M10. Pin the deletion of the source: RF-03, SF-13, EX-41, RF-01 (`cwd_files` equals []), plus decisions 0018 P6/0035 and README. Pin 'one function, no own rules in the team core': TM-44 (team-journal.test.js, reads only tools/src/team/*.js at the top level: store.js must have a single-line `import ... pixel-office/mask.js";`, and no file there may contain AKIA, ASIA, github_pat, -----BEGIN, `sk-[`, `gh[pos]` or the label text), TM-04 (team-state.test.js:151, the number of places that write files, found by the words writeFile/appendFile/createWriteStream; removeSource uses unlinkSync and is not counted). MUST STAY GREEN BECAUSE maskSecrets is not to change under either fix of ISS-0093: HK-21 and its rows (MASK_RULE_ROWS M1-M10 incl. M7-jwt, M7-no-eyJ, M7-file `см. a.test.js` -> label, M10-base64, M10-40; MASK_KEEP_ROWS; idempotence on 10000 seeded inputs) and HK-24 (pixel-office-hook.test.js:903, :1025), MK-01..MK-05 (hook, server, panels), NM-06, TM-43 second test, the team-journal and team-store text-field tests, the planner tests of acceptedBlock. HK-21/HK-24/MK-01/MK-03 were run by name on the base: 4 of 4 pass; the others of the Pixel Office files bind ports and were not run by me.

ONE DESIGN OR TWO FIXES: TWO FIXES, IN THIS ORDER. 1) ISS-0093 first (HIGH; data loss). It needs no change of the meaning of maskSecrets: a new exported entry for file content in mask.js, built from the same rule functions (M1-M6, M8, M9 and a JWT-shape rule instead of M7; M10 per I8), used by store.js:395 and by runner.js:132 - both, the same function, or depsOf keeps corrupting (R5) - plus the notice to the user, the README paragraphs (253, 391 and the masking section), a decision record (Q12; it touches 0013/0017), a criterion (I9) and the tests of I6 by the 'was -> became' table. maskSecrets, HK-21, HK-24, MK-*, the Pixel Office and journal text stay as they are. 2) Then ISS-0058 together with ISS-0045 (MEDIUM/LOW; same function, same file names in acceptedBlock): it does change maskSecrets (M7 host/file-name look-alikes, M10 on long roles), must change the pinned rows M7-file and the 'consequence of M7' paragraph of README and decision 0013 by a table, and is a Q7 trade (less masking of text in the journal that is seen on a page) that needs its own record. Why not one design: different severity, different tests (8 pinned tests of files against HK-21 family of text), different decisions, and ISS-0058 can lower detection while ISS-0093 does not have to; one design would make a HIGH data-loss fix wait for a Q7 discussion. They must not run in parallel: write sets overlap in tools/src/pixel-office/mask.js, tools/README.md (masking paragraphs), tools/test/pixel-office-helpers.js. The JWT-shape rule written in ISS-0093 is the thing ISS-0058 can reuse to narrow M7 for text.

FOR THE FIX DESIGN (step 3): what must change, not how. Behaviour: (1) the content of a result file is stored in files/, and handed to the reviewer and to dependent tasks, unchanged byte for byte except for what is a secret by the precise patterns: PEM block, Authorization value, user:password in an address, keys with known prefixes (sk-, ghp_/gho_/ghs_, github_pat_, AKIA/ASIA), Bearer values, name=value pairs of M9 - and a JWT recognised by its shape (eyJ + three base64url parts), so TM-43's JWT bait stays hidden (Q7). Any three-part token (versions, hosts, a.test.js, obj.prop.method) is NOT a secret in a file. (2) store.js #publish and runner.js depsOf use the same single entry; the entry lives in mask.js (TM-44), the team core gets no rule text. (3) When something in a file was replaced, the user is told (a notice or a field - the 37-event catalogue and the RESULT_FILE shape decide; this is a design choice) and the reviewer text says that the file was changed; today nothing is said. (4) The source in work/: the rule 'removed after acceptance' (0018 P6, REQ-010 16, REQ-013 14/15) can stay as it is: once the stored copy is exact, deleting the source loses nothing; where a secret was replaced, deleting it is the point of P6. Keeping sources in work/ is NOT needed for this defect (see I10). (5) Questions to put to the owner or to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Q7 cannot be lowered): M10 (32+ characters with a lower-case letter and a digit or capital) on files catches secrets without a prefix (an `sk_live_` style token, `xoxb-` tokens) but also hits lockfile integrity strings and long identifiers; dropping it for files widens the residual risk named in README, keeping it leaves a smaller corruption (package-lock.json: 27 marks, tools/src: 0). My recommendation to put forward: keep M10 for files unless a recorded decision of the owner says otherwise, and name the integrity strings of lockfiles as the one exception to check. (6) Files: tools/src/pixel-office/mask.js (new entry only), tools/src/team/store.js, tools/src/team/runner.js, tools/README.md (253, 391, the masking section), a new record in decisions/, the criterion of I9, tests of I6/I11. Not to touch: maskSecrets semantic, M7/M10 as text rules, the Pixel Office files, the 37-event catalogue unless (3) needs it.

WF-03 STEP 2 (WF-01 FIRST): the expected behaviour is written nowhere. REQ-010 criterion 16(б) says only that the secret sample is replaced by the label; REQ-013 14/15 say the source is removed and the reviewer/dependents get the file; REQ-009 criterion 12 is about events. No criterion and no test says that ordinary text, code and version numbers of a result file stay unchanged, nor what the user is told when something is replaced. REQ-ANALYST must add such a criterion (a micro-amendment of REQ-010 16(б) or a new criterion of REQ-013) with the check by command and the oracle with literal expected strings (not by `maskSecrets(text)`); REQ-VALIDATOR checks it. Also: ISS-0093 cites 'REQ-009 criterion 12' - the correct citation is REQ-010 criterion 16(б) and REQ-013 criteria 14 and 15 (DOC-UPDATER to correct the defect text).

Q13, an entry for docs/anti-patterns.md (text for DOC-UPDATER): 'A masking function written for short lines of text was reused for the full content of files, and every test checked only that the secret bait is gone, never that ordinary content is kept.' What happened: M7 and M10 (decision 0013, lines of owner requests, extra masking = safe side) were applied to result files (0017 P9); the guard tests have key baits only; TM-43 'masking does not touch ids, codes, hashes and names' writes `Версия 1.2.3` and does not read the content back; two tests use the function under test as the oracle. How to do it right: a mechanism for another kind of data gets its own analysis of what it changes in ordinary data of that kind; a masking test has two halves - the secret is gone AND a fixed list of ordinary samples (code, versions, hosts, file names) is byte-equal, with literal expected strings; an oracle is never the function under test.
